messages:
emily-cs: :rotating_light: Support ticket (#42378) — customer reporting a spike of 500s from the /v1/generate endpoint when they exceed quota. They say it used to return 429 but now random 500/504s. Customer pasted a sample response: `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` with body `\"error: rate limiter failure\"`. They can reproduce consistently for requests that should be blocked by quota.

liz-support: I verified with the ticket's request-id header (rid: abc123). Repro steps from their report:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Project: acme" \
  -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
They also included a couple of raw headers showing `x-redwood-route: quota` then a 500.

jonah-eng-runtime: tagging in. Can you drop the request-id and timestamps? I want to check the gateway logs and quota-service traces.

emily-cs: request-id abc123, original capture attached to ticket. Customer is on Hosted (us-west). This started ~2026-05-02 13:40 UTC.

jonah-eng-runtime: pulled the gateway trace for abc123. Short summary: request routed to quota-service v2, quota-service made a downstream call to quota-cache (redis cluster), that call hit a connection timeout, quota-service returned a 502-ish internal error that the gateway forwarded as 500.

jonah-eng-runtime: Relevant trace snippet:
```
gateway -> quota-service/v2 [200ms]
quota-service -> quota-cache (redis): TCP connect timeout after 1000ms
quota-service: unhandled error: redis transport timeout -> returning 500
gateway: proxied status 500 to client
```

paul-infra: Alerts show a burst of redis connection timeouts in us-west cluster around 13:39-13:45 UTC. Same window as customer. Looks like ephemeral network flaps to the redis replica set. That should have been handled by quota-service with a 429 for quota decisions, not a 500 for dependency failures.

maria-sre: root cause hypothesis: quota-service is returning 5xx on dependency timeouts and gateway is blindly propagating that to clients. We want quota failures (decision that user exceeded quota) to be 429; dependency failures should be 502/503 and ideally the gateway should map quota-service dependency timeouts to a safe 429 for requests that would have been rate limited? Hmm — we need to decide correct behavior. For user-facing, if quota-service cannot make a definitive decision, returning 500 is worse than 429.

jonah-eng-runtime: +1. We have a misroute too: some requests are hitting an older quota-service instance (v1) that lacks the newer resiliency code path. Routing rule `quota->primary` sometimes resolves to the legacy pool when primary is overloaded. That's probably why only some requests got 429 and others 500.

liz-support: Customer impact: intermittent 5xx for quota-exceeded flows. They asked for ETA and mitigation. 

paul-infra: quick mitigation options:
- Update gateway to map quota-service 5xx that contain text `rate limiter` or `quota` to 429 before forwarding to client (fast, low-risk).
- Hotflip routing so all quota decisions use the resilient pool (v2) only (higher risk but direct).
- Increase redis connection pool / fallback to standby cache (requires infra change, medium risk).

maria-sre: I recommend first: gateway mapping rule + an ops-level circuit-breaker on quota-service upstream so gateway returns 429 for currently flagged tenant IDs while we heal redis. Then roll routing changes.

jonah-eng-runtime: I'll prepare a tiny gateway patch: map responses from quota-service where response code >=500 AND body contains case-insensitive regex `(rate limiter|quota|quota-service|quota decision)` -> rewrite to 429 + body `{\"error\": \"quota exceeded\"}`. We'll do canary in us-west.

jonah-eng-runtime: repro steps I used locally to simulate (for engineering):
```
# simulate quota-service dependency timeout
nc -l 9999 & # fake redis that never responds
# run gateway with local config -> send identical request, expect 500 from old behavior
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer FAKE" -d '{"input":"x"}' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -v
```
liz-support: Can you also provide a customer-friendly blurb we can send before full fix? They want something to post to their engineering Slack.

emily-cs: Suggested message to customer: "We're aware some quota-exceeded requests are returning 5xx. We're rolling a gateway mitigation to ensure quota cases return 429 while we fix an upstream cache instability. No action required on your side. ETA ~30-45m for mitigation rollout."

deploy-bot: :gear: Starting canary deploy `gateway/patch-quota-map` to us-west (instance set: 2 of 20) by jonah-eng-runtime.

alerts-bot: :information_source: redis-us-west-1: increased connection failures observed, 13:38-13:47 UTC (peak 4.3% failures).

jonah-eng-runtime: Canary logs look good — rewritten responses are returning 429 for the simulated budget-exceeded case and normal requests still 200. Kicking rollout to 25% now.

deploy-bot: :rocket: Rollout `gateway/patch-quota-map` to 25% complete.

paul-infra: I also disabled the legacy quota-service in routing table (temporary) to force v2 for new traffic. That's a sticky choice; revert in 2 hours if any regressions.

emily-cs: Customer updated: sent the note and included monitoring link. They replied: "Thanks, we're seeing fewer 500s already." :thumbsup:

maria-sre: After 40m, redis cluster showed recovery. Connection failure rate dropped back to baseline. We should keep the mapping rule for an hour then revert. Also open follow-up: improve quota-service to map dependency timeouts internally to a consistent 429/503 decision and add better health-check routing to avoid legacy misroute.

jonah-eng-runtime: Filed a follow-up JIRA: INF-9981 (quota-service: unify error mapping + harden routing). Also adding unit tests to ensure any 'quota decision unresolved' flows are translated at the service layer, not only at gateway.

paul-infra: Postmortem todo: we need a runbook entry: if quota-service returns 5xx and alerts spike on redis, route to v2 and enable gateway mapping. I'll draft and link.

liz-support: Final customer update sent: "We deployed a mitigation that ensures quota-related failures return 429; we also applied routing changes to prefer the resilient quota pool. We're monitoring and will follow up with RCA and permanent fixes."

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollout complete: `gateway/patch-quota-map` at 100%.
